subject: ROOT CAUSE of 'one job per wait / seqw=0 in every window': the kernel rejected the bridge's WAIT_SEQ(0,0) availability probe, so async submission has NEVER been enabled on the device. Fix = kernel 0108 (1 hunk)
body: lag-analysis REPORT says jobs run strictly one per wait and early_wait=0, seqw=0 everywhere. Source chain: compute_frontend tegu_async_configure -> n2mb_async(conn,1) sets b->async=2 -> async_probe() sends WAIT_SEQ(seq=0,timeout=0) and enables async only if the call SUCCEEDS with n==3 && out[0]==4 (bridge comment line 126: 'WAIT_SEQ(0,0) only answers on a kernel that has it (nothing to reap)'; the bridge test's fake kernel returns [4,0,0] for seq 0). The real kernel (my 0090) had n2c_seq_state() return N2C_E_NO_JOB for seq==0 (and my own core test asserted that), i.e. kIOReturnNotFound -> probe fails -> b->async=0 forever -> every jm_submit does SEL_WAIT right away: exactly 'waits=n, seqw=0'. Contract mismatch, kernel side was wrong. 0108 (patch df8478f4, gpu/build/kernel-p1-20261026): seq 0 = vacuous success {pending 0, done 0, failed 0} in n2c_seq_state; core test updated (22 scenarios PASS, ASan/UBSan). Image to verify: gpu/build/device-mmu-p11-candidate/ui654fb60seq (kernel with 0100-0108, n2fbhz=60), building now; expected first line change: NORD2 GPU JOBS seqw=<waits>/<jobs>/.. non-zero and waits= much lower than n. CAUTION for render/encode (a9f7): this switches the whole async path ON for the first time on a device - it was only ever exercised against the bridge-test model. Things to check in the first log: (1) the kernel in-flight window (96 jobs per ctx, SUBMIT_JM answers kIOReturnBusy beyond it; the bridge reaps once and resubmits), (2) release while jobs are unreaped is busy-consumed (handle gone, free deferred) - bridge handles it per its test, (3) any code that reads GPU-written memory right after a draw must go through the 'sync' diagnostics path, (4) with TEGU_ASYNC_PIPELINE_DEFAULT=0 the command still waits once at teguFinishGPU (wait_pending -> WAIT_SEQ), which is what fix #1 of the report asks for; 'scheduled' early signal and 2 frames in flight are separate frontend work. Kernel support for 'many jobs per submission' is NOT needed beyond this: jobs of one context already execute in submission order, WAIT_SEQ reaps a whole command with one call, my 0100 (no connection lock during waits) matters once a finish thread exists.
